forms.label: Past polite

definitions.gloss: to be conscious of; to be aware of
definitions.explanation: To deliberately pay attention to or be mindful of something. Used when someone becomes aware of or focuses on something they might otherwise overlook.

definitions.gloss: to be self-conscious about; to be attracted to
definitions.explanation: To become nervously aware of someone, typically due to romantic interest. Used when someone starts feeling awkward or attracted to another person.

examples.japanese: {健康|けんこう}を{意識|いしき}して{生活|せいかつ}する。
examples.english: Live with awareness of your health.

examples.japanese: {環境問題|かんきょうもんだい}を{意識|いしき}する{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えてきた。
examples.english: More people are becoming conscious of environmental issues.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}を{意識|いしき}しながら、{効率|こうりつ}よく{仕事|しごと}を{進|すす}めた。
examples.english: I progressed with work efficiently while being mindful of the time.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}を{意識|いしき}してしまう。
examples.english: I can't help being self-conscious around him.

examples.japanese: {褒|ほ}められてから、{彼女|かのじょ}のことを{意識|いしき}するようになった。
examples.english: After being complimented by her, I started to be aware of her in a romantic way.

examples.japanese: {最初|さいしょ}はただの{友達|ともだち}だったが、いつの{間|ま}にか{彼|かれ}のことを{意識|いしき}するようになっていた。
examples.english: At first we were just friends, but before I knew it I had started to be conscious of him romantically.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 is used broadly in daily life, business, and self-improvement contexts. Sense 2 is very common in romantic contexts and often appears in manga, dramas, and conversation among young people.
The noun {意識|いしき} alone means "consciousness" or "awareness" and is also used in medical contexts ({意識|いしき}がない = unconscious).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {健康|けんこう}を{意識|いしき}する (be health-conscious)
- {時間|じかん}を{意識|いしき}する (be mindful of time)
- {相手|あいて}を{意識|いしき}する (become aware of someone romantically)
- {意識|いしき}し{始|はじ}める (start becoming conscious of)
- {無意識|むいしき}に (unconsciously — opposite)
